Name: Hanmer Home Base (Start)
Description: Expedition departure point (4671 Dupuis Drive, Hanmer, ON). Full 87 & 91 fuel tanks.

Name: Motel au P'tit Sapin (Mirabel)
Description: Ground-level roadside motel on Route 117 in Mirabel. Room-front exterior motorcycle parking right outside your door.

Name: Motel Le Mirabeau (Mirabel)
Description: Clean, comfortable roadside motel fallback on Route 117 in Mirabel.

Name: Super 8 by Wyndham Saint-Jérôme / Mirabel
Description: Convenient fallback motor hotel off Hwy 117 / A-15 gateway.

Name: Camping Mirabel
Description: Lush wooded private campground with pool and hot showers in Mirabel.

Name: Carillon Canal National Historic Lock
Description: Historic 19th-century military canal on the Ottawa River built after the War of 1812 with a massive 20-metre single hydraulic guillotine lock.

Name: Sturgeon Falls Shell
Description: Hwy 17 full service Shell with V-Power 91 Premium.

Name: Deep River Canadian Tire Gas+
Description: Trans-Canada Hwy 17 backup station with 91 Premium.

Name: Pembroke Esso / Circle K
Description: Major Hwy 17 fuel stop before crossing Chenaux Dam into Quebec.

Name: Shawville Petro-Canada
Description: Route 148 fuel in the heart of Pontiac county.

Name: Thurso Ultramar
Description: Route 148 Ottawa River backup station with 91 Premium.

Name: Montebello Shell
Description: Scenic Route 148 Ottawa River corridor fuel.

Name: Mirabel Ultramar (Route 117)
Description: Convenient fuel top-off right next to Motel au P'tit Sapin.

Name: Petawawa Shell (Hwy 17)
Description: Strategic backup station on Hwy 17 eastbound 20 km before Pembroke.

Name: Portage-du-Fort Ottawa River Crossing
Description: Historic Chenaux Generating Station dam bridge crossing the Ottawa River from Ontario into Quebec.

Name: Route 148 Scenic River Corridor (Gatineau to Fassett)
Description: Winding, scenic motorcycle corridor along the north shore of the Ottawa River through St-Philippe and Lachute into Mirabel.

Name: The Nook Creperie (Pembroke)
Description: Charming downtown Pembroke creperie serving sweet & savory buckwheat crepes, paninis, and espresso — ideal Day 1 lunch stop along Hwy 17.

Name: Twiggs Coffee Roasters (North Bay — Hwy 17)
Description: 473 Fraser St / McKeown Ave, North Bay, ON. Famous Northern Ontario micro-roaster — fresh espresso, baked scones, and rider breakfast stop on Day 1 & Day 18.

Name: Tim Hortons (Sturgeon Falls — Hwy 17)
Description: Front St / Trans-Canada Hwy 17, Sturgeon Falls, ON. First morning coffee stop east of Hanmer.

Name: Tim Hortons (Mattawa — Hwy 17)
Description: Main St / Hwy 17, Mattawa, ON. Convenient coffee & restroom stop at the confluence of the Mattawa and Ottawa rivers.

Name: Tim Hortons (Pembroke — Hwy 17)
Description: Pembroke St W, Pembroke, ON. Quick coffee & snack stop along the Ottawa Valley corridor.

Name: Starbucks (Pembroke — Pembroke Mall)
Description: 1100 Pembroke St E, Pembroke, ON. Espresso & cold brew stop right along the Ottawa River corridor.

Name: Tim Hortons (Mirabel — Route 117)
Description: 13425 Bd Curé-Labelle, Mirabel, QC. Right beside Day 1 lodging for Day 2 07:00 AM rollout coffee.

Name: Travelodge by Wyndham Baie-Comeau
Description: Clean, highly-rated rider-friendly motor inn directly on Route 138. Easy ground-floor motorcycle parking.

Name: Hôtel Le Manoir Baie-Comeau
Description: Historic stone manor overlooking the St. Lawrence River.

Name: Parc national du Fjord-du-Saguenay (Tadoussac)
Description: Spectacular fjord park with marine mammal lookouts and coastal camping.

Name: Phare du Moulin-à-Baude (Tadoussac)
Description: Historic red-and-white coastal beacon perched above the St. Lawrence estuary and Saguenay Fjord confluence; world-class beluga whale lookout.

Name: Phare de Cap-de-Bon-Désir
Description: Historic navigational station on granite ledges dropping 300 meters into the St. Lawrence Laurentian Channel; prime shore whale watching.

Name: Phare de Pointe-des-Monts
Description: Erected 1830, one of the oldest circular stone lighthouses in North America; marks entrance to the Gulf of St. Lawrence with museum.

Name: Port-au-Persil Waterfall & Historic Chapel
Description: Hidden Charlevoix cove off Route 138 where a fresh mountain waterfall cascades directly over granite rocks into the saltwater St. Lawrence estuary.

Name: Berthierville Esso
Description: Route 138 Chemin du Roy backup station with 91 Premium.

Name: Trois-Rivières Shell
Description: Chemin du Roy (Route 138) mid-stage top-off.

Name: Baie-Saint-Paul Shell
Description: Route 138 Charlevoix gateway backup station with 91 Premium.

Name: Les Escoumins Shell
Description: Route 138 North Shore backup station with 91 Premium.

Name: Baie-Comeau Shell V-Power Hub
Description: CRITICAL: Mandatory top-off for both bikes and auxiliary fuel bladder before entering remote QC-389. Shell V-Power 91 available.

Name: Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré Irving
Description: Route 138 Côte-de-Beaupré strategic backup station before Charlevoix mountains.

Name: Tadoussac Pétro-T
Description: Strategic backup station directly at the mouth of the Saguenay Fjord / ferry landing.

Name: Forestville Crevier
Description: Route 138 North Shore strategic backup station between Les Escoumins and Baie-Comeau.

Name: Tadoussac Fjord Ferry (Route 138)
Description: Free 10-minute year-round ferry crossing across the mouth of the Saguenay Fjord. Motorcyclists directed to front of queue.

Name: Boulevard Champlain & Cap Diamant River Parkway
Description: Stunning river-level motorcycle boulevard curving beneath the towering cliffs of Quebec City and Château Frontenac.

Name: Autoroute 50 & Route 138 North Shore Scenic Corridor
Description: Historic Chemin du Roy and Côte-de-Beaupré bypassing Montreal and Hwy 40 entirely.

Name: Microbrasserie Le Temps d'une Pinte (Trois-Rivières)
Description: Award-winning Trois-Rivières craft microbrewery and kitchen bistrot serving artisanal Quebec cuisine and house-roasted coffee.

Name: St-Pancrace — Microbrasserie / Le Pub (Baie-Comeau)
Description: 55 Pl. la Salle, Baie-Comeau. Celebrated Côte-Nord craft brewpub featuring boreal-inspired ales and hearty pub fare before launching up QC-389.

Name: Pêcherie Manicouagan Inc (Baie-Comeau)
Description: 334 Bd la Salle, Baie-Comeau. Fresh St. Lawrence snow crab, Nordic shrimp, smoked salmon, and coastal seafood market.

Name: Starbucks (Trois-Rivières — Hwy 40)
Description: 4520 Bd des Forges, Trois-Rivières, QC. Quick espresso stop off Autoroute 40.

Name: Tim Hortons (Beaupré / Sainte-Anne-de-Beaupré — Route 138)
Description: 10620 Bd Sainte-Anne, Beaupré, QC. Right on Route 138 before climbing into the Charlevoix highlands.

Name: Tim Hortons (La Malbaie — Route 138)
Description: 375 Bd de Comporté, La Malbaie, QC. Coffee & warm-up stop along the St. Lawrence north shore.

Name: Hotel Wabush
Description: Safe, warm, rider-friendly hotel in Labrador West. On-site restaurant, high-speed WiFi, bear-safe protection.

Name: Two Seasons Inn (Labrador City)
Description: Full service hotel in Labrador City with dining and heated facilities.

Name: Manic-5 (Daniel-Johnson Dam)
Description: World's largest multiple-arch hollow buttress dam. 214 m high, 1.3 km wide. Marvel of modern engineering.

Name: Gagnon Ghost Town (Abandoned Boreal Streets)
Description: Km 485 on QC-389. Thriving 1970s mining city demolished in 1985. Concrete sidewalks and street curbs still intact in the forest.

Name: Fermont Windbreak Wall ('Le Mur')
Description: Famous 1.3 km long, 5-story windbreak building sheltering the subarctic mining community from freezing arctic gales.

Name: Manic-5 Fuel (Motel de l'Énergie)
Description: Km 214 on QC-389. Essential fuel stop next to Daniel-Johnson Dam. 87 Octane ONLY. Use bladder siphon or Lucas booster for Ducati.

Name: Relais Gabriel Fuel Outpost
Description: Km 316 on QC-389. Mandatory fuel top-up on eastern Manicouagan crater rim. 87 Octane ONLY. Use bladder siphon or Lucas booster for Ducati.

Name: Fermont Shell
Description: Km 565 on QC-389. Full service Shell in Fermont mining town.

Name: Labrador City Ultramar Hub
Description: Full city fuel station, Tim Hortons, hardware store.

Name: Zone Camping Relais de Gabriel
Description: Wilderness camping backup zone at Relais Gabriel (km 318 of Route 389) right after the Manic-5 to Relais Gabriel gravel stretch.

Name: Station Uapishka — Monts Groulx (Hotel Backup)
Description: UNESCO Manicouagan-Uapishka Biosphere Reserve eco-lodge, inn, and outfitter backup at the base of the Monts Groulx (km 336 of QC-389).

Name: Campement Modulaire (Mont-Wright / QC-389)
Description: Modular camp facility near Mont-Wright and the southern approach to Fermont on Route 389.

Name: Pourvoirie Lac Justone Fermont | Rivière Caniapiscau
Description: Outfitter cabin and wilderness camping backup on Lac Justone just west of Fermont on Route 389.

Name: Duley Lake Provincial Park Campground
Description: Scenic lakeside provincial park campground between the Québec/Labrador border and Labrador City / Wabush.

Name: Trish’s Place (Wabush / Labrador City B&B Backup)
Description: Welcoming local guesthouse and B&B lodging backup in Wabush / Labrador City.

Name: Gateway Labrador — Visitor Information Centre w/ Campsites
Description: Labrador West visitor centre, museum, and RV/tent camping backup right on Route 500 in Labrador City.

Name: Stationnement Harfang-Nord (Monts Groulx Trailhead Parking)
Description: Official Monts Groulx Harfang-Nord trailhead parking & emergency highway stopping area on QC-389.

Name: Stationnement Départ Monts Groulx Nord/Sud
Description: Official Monts Groulx North/South trailhead parking lot & safe roadside pullout on QC-389.

Description: Extra-large graded gravel roadside staging & emergency parking area along Route 389.

Name: Pourvoirie Relais Gabriel Restaurant (Hwy 389)
Description: Iconic wilderness outfitter dining room at km 318 of Route 389 serving hot rider meals, soup, and coffee in the heart of the Côte-Nord.

Name: Iron Rock Brewing Co. (Labrador City)
Description: Labrador's premier craft brewery in Labrador City (118 Humphrey Rd) — great post-QC-389 celebration taproom and food stop.

Name: Baba Q's Smoke & Grill (Labrador City)
Description: Authentic slow-smoked brisket, ribs, pulled pork, and hearty platters in Labrador City.

Name: Tim Hortons (Baie-Comeau — Bd Laflèche)
Description: 855 Bd Laflèche, Baie-Comeau, QC. Essential final Tim Hortons coffee & breakfast stop before turning north onto Route 389 toward Manic-5!

Name: Belvédère Réservoir Manicouagan (QC-389 Viewpoint)
Description: Panoramic highway overlook beside the Manicouagan Reservoir ('Eye of Québec' annular impact crater lake) north of Manic-5 Dam.

Name: Gagnon Airport (Former Mining Town Runway — QC-389)
Description: Abandoned airstrip and hauntingly flat highway corridor of the former iron-mining town of Gagnon (closed and dismantled in 1985) along Route 389.

Name: QC-389 Off-Road Side-of-Road Viewpoint
Description: Elevated side-of-road gravel pull-off viewpoint overlooking the subarctic Côte-Nord valleys and lakes.

Name: QC-389 Emergency Highway Telephone Booth
Description: Remote emergency satellite/landline highway telephone booth on Route 389 south of Fire Lake.

Name: 🚁 Drone Launch Spot: Fire Lake Iron Mine
Description: Designated roadside pullout to launch the drone for dramatic aerial footage of the ArcelorMittal Fire Lake open-pit iron mine and QC-389.

Name: 🚁 Drone Launch Spot: Mont-Wright Mega-Mine
Description: Prime roadside vantage point to fly the drone overlooking the colossal Mont-Wright open-pit iron ore mining complex near Fermont.

Name: 📸 Fermont Welcome Sign
Description: Photo-op stop at the town entrance sign for Fermont, QC (home of the famous 1.3 km wind-screening 'Le Mur-Écran' building).

Name: 📸 Québec Provincial Border Sign (QC-389 / NL-500)
Description: Iconic 'Bonjour Québec' border sign at the 53rd parallel dividing Québec (Route 389) and Labrador (Route 500).

Name: 📸 Welcome to Labrador Border Sign (South)
Description: Mandatory rider photo stop at the 'Welcome to Labrador / Bienvenue au Labrador' border monument entering Newfoundland & Labrador!

Name: 📸 Labrador Border Sign (North Pullout)
Description: Northern pullout side of the Québec–Labrador border crossing on Route 500.

Name: Crystal Falls Hiking Trail (Labrador City)
Description: Scenic short hike overlooking cascading Crystal Falls between the Labrador border and Labrador City.

Name: Harrie Lake Trail (Labrador West)
Description: Peaceful boreal lakeside walking trail near Labrador City and Wabush.

Name: The Truck — Giant Terex Mining Dump Truck Display
Description: Colossal retired open-pit iron ore haul truck on display in Labrador City — classic motorcycle scale photo-op!

Name: Smokey Mountain Ski & Recreational Area
Description: Labrador City's alpine ski hill and scenic high-point overlook just northwest of town.

Name: Jean Lake Walking Trail (Wabush)
Description: 5.5 km groomed boardwalk and gravel walking trail looping around Jean Lake between Wabush and Labrador City.
